title: pm-dispatch SKILL: five measured lessons from the 2026-08-10 services shift (queue-kick signature, arm-timing variant, opportunistic restart conditions, claim-race arbitration, lane inventory reading)
body:
Filed at shift handoff by the `domain:services` seat (#6021, session `session_015fkdTyGmMD5s8ZtEifvuGy`), per the seat-exit checklist's standing product. **Unassigned, no labels — routing and grading are the triage seat's territory.**

Twelve cards landed this shift (all MERGED), plus four standby-period dispositions. These five are the lessons the existing SKILL text does not already carry. Each is measured on a named card, not recalled.

⚠️ **Provenance to read first, so nobody re-litigates it**: items 1–3 overlap the content of **PR #7410**, which I opened and which was **closed**. It was closed because I misread the maintainer's 「更新最新的项目经理技能」 as *edit the skill* when it meant *load the latest skill* — the notes' substance was never ruled on. Filing them here as **suggestions for the maintainer/triage to judge**, which is the protocol's product, not as an edit. Two mechanical facts that PR also established, worth having on the record: a `.claude/`-only PR takes the **`skip-changeset` label** (an empty changeset is rejected by #5471), and `SKILL.md` is under a **line ratchet** (`check:pm-skill-ratchet`, ceiling 3050) — so narrative belongs in `references/incidents.md`, not the hot file. Any accepted item below should land that way.

---

### 1. Queue-kick signature: no `merge_group` run of the PR's own = queue-rebuild collateral, not a red

Measured on **#7311**. A PR was removed from the merge queue while Actions held **no `merge_group` run belonging to it** (its batch-mates' runs were all `success`). That is a queue rebuild cancelling it in passing, not a failure. One receipted flip re-queue landed it.

Suggested prescription: re-queue **once**, leaving a signature-reading receipt on the PR (which runs were read, why it reads as rebuild collateral) so the queue steward's ledger can reconcile it; a **second** kick on the same PR hands off to the steward (#5810). ⛔ Never re-queue without the receipt — an un-receipted re-queue is indistinguishable from a flaky hard-retry in the steward's table.

### 2. The empty-field arm receipt has a second timing shape — and the "fix" can drop the flag off an already-queued PR

The existing note 21 covers: arming a green `clean` PR returns an **empty-field receipt** (`method: , enabled at `) and the PR does not enqueue; flip `disable`→`enable` once. Confirmed at scale this shift — **8 for 8**, every instance landed.

**New (measured on #7446):** after a ready-flip, arming can return that same empty receipt and the PR **enqueues anyway, immediately**. A `disable` issued after that does **not** remove queue membership (only converting to draft does) but **does** clear the auto-merge flag. Net effect: the PR lands normally, but if it is later kicked it will not re-arm itself. Suggested addition: **read the queue branch before treating an empty receipt as "not enqueued"** — the receipt is not evidence either way, and the corrective flip is only correct when the branch is genuinely absent.

### 3. Opportunistic restart conditions fail silently — hang them on claim/dispatch, not on the passer-by

The sharpest one, and it generalises. **#5536** carries restart condition ② in the classic form: *"or the next PR that touches any of these three seam files keeps `source` as a same-function wrap-up."* Triage has now recorded that condition firing **four times** without being taken (#6042, `e2798fa`, `d538647fc`, `06be54ec3` — two of them on 2026-08-10 alone), each time by someone already inside the file who had no reason to know the card existed.

The failure is structural, not negligence: a condition phrased as *"someone will do it while they're in there"* has **no reader at the moment it fires**. Suggested rule: a held finding whose restart condition is opportunistic must name the **files** that trigger it, and the owning lane must carry a *dispatch-time* check — the dispatch prompt for any card touching those files names the finding and asks for the ride-along as a declared out-of-surface addition. The lane seat post is where that check has to live to survive a handoff. (Done for #5536 this shift: seat post #6021 gained a 「派发前必查」 section, and the commitment is public on #5536.)

### 4. Same-account claim races are arbitrated by claim-comment session ID + timestamp only

Measured on **#7145**: two sessions on the same GitHub identity assigned and posted claims **69 seconds apart**. The `assignee` field carries zero information between them — it reads as "mine" to both. The only tiebreaker is the claim comments' timestamps and session IDs; first comment wins.

Suggested addition to the claim-race clause: the loser's duty does not end at standing down — it posts a **handoff comment** carrying the readings it already took (in-flight sibling PRs, region declarations, serial constraints cleared), so the winner does not re-scan. This is the PM-to-PM form of CLAUDE.md's re-read-the-comments rule. (Note the multi-account caveat already in the skill: across *different* accounts, `assignee` does answer "who" and none of this applies.)

### 5. Lane inventory: field-narrowed `list_issues` over `search_issues` — the query shape decides what you can see

Two things this shift, one of them a real miss:

- **Output cost**: `list_issues` with `labels: [domain:X]`, `fields: [number, labels, updated_at]` returns the lane's whole open set with no bodies — roughly an order of magnitude cheaper than `search_issues`, which returns full bodies.
- **The miss it caught**: I had been querying `label:domain:services label:pm:queue no:assignee` every round and reporting **decision box: 0**. That was wrong — **#7243** had been sitting in the lane with `needs-user-decision` the whole time. A query scoped to one pm-state cannot see the others, and the round report's three health metrics span several. Reading the **whole lane and intersecting locally** makes every pm-state visible in one read and cannot produce this class of blind spot.

---

### Not a SKILL change — a tooling card someone should file separately

`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` derives gate families from changed paths, and it **does not surface `check:engine-double-contract`** for a card that introduces a new engine double. Measured: **PR #7446** ran the derived gates locally, went green, and then took an ESLint red in CI naming exactly that gate on both new test files. The dispatch prompt is the only place that gap can be closed today, which puts it on the PM's memory — the failure mode the deriver exists to remove. Splitting this out rather than folding it in, since it is a script defect, not skill text.

---

Dedup: searched open issues for pm-dispatch/SKILL suggestion cards before filing — **#7493** (release board vs file-at-destination, cloud) and **#7498** (four-lens block on decision cards) are the near neighbours; neither covers any item above.
